limitations: Rising aggregate spending can coexist with falling unit costs.

from_speaker: It has not succeeded in reducing costs so far
reducing prices would only increase costs
our_interpretation: The plain contextual reading concerns OpenAI's own expenditure, rather than the prices its customers pay.
The historical comparison covers the early-2023 baseline discussed in the post through July 29, 2024. It does not concern full-year 2024 realized expenditure.
The wider post expressly bases its cost discussion on reporting and estimates, so the accounting basis is estimate; no GAAP or other formal basis is asserted.
Total expenditure and cost per unit of inference are both plausible meanings of costs. They must not be substituted for one another.
The second clause asserts a necessary causal increase in total costs following price cuts, presumably through greater usage. So far is a temporal qualifier, not a conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable estimates of actual internal expenditure establish no reduction through the post, and evidence linking price cuts, additional usage and costs establishes the asserted necessary increase.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable estimates establish a reduction in the relevant internal costs, or a well-supported price-cut episode shows that total costs did not necessarily increase. Customer price reductions alone do not qualify.

evidence.explanation: The article reports the failure of an intended efficiency improvement, citing The Information. Failure of one project does not establish that all cost-reduction efforts failed or measure total expenditure.

OpenAI advertised improved cost efficiency before the post. The announcement describes API affordability and supplies no comparable internal expenditure series, so it cannot decisively contradict the financial claim.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable internal-cost records or well-sourced estimates through July 2024, plus evidence measuring how price cuts changed usage and expenditure after accounting for efficiency improvements and fixed commitments.
